entries.title: How Damage Works
entries.summary: How one hit goes from swing to health loss

blocks.text: This page explains how much health one of your hits actually takes off. The takeaways below are all you need to start; the full formula is at the end. Unfamiliar words: see [[start/glossary]].

rows: Gives a weapon its own <t>stat panel</t> (a set of random base stats) so it can hold mods. Ordinary weapons are consecrated at the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}
A weapon dropped by the boss {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}; it comes already consecrated
An upgrade card slotted into a weapon (not a Minecraft mod); each stat line on the card is an attribute

blocks.text: Key Takeaways

items: Only damage from a consecrated weapon in your main hand gets mod bonuses; unconsecrated weapons use plain vanilla damage.
Every hit has a <t>physical</t> part and an <t>elemental</t> part. <w>Crits only boost the physical part</w>; bane boosts both.

Swing melee weapons at full charge: below full charge, vanilla already lowers the damage, and then the physical and elemental multipliers are scaled down by the charge again — a half-charged swing deals only about a fifth of a full-charge hit.
Damage never goes below 0, however many negative attributes you stack.

items.text: Armor, shields and other reductions come last; damage numbers show the health actually lost after them.
Armor, shields and other reductions come last.

blocks.text: From Swing to Health Loss

items: Classify: you hit the target yourself (sweep hits included) → melee; an arrow, projectile or bullet you fired hit it → ranged.
Add damage bonuses: melee and ranged each use their own bonus attributes — see the table at the end.
Sum the elements: the Kuva weapon's innate element + every elemental attribute (see [[combat/elements]]).
Multiply by {lang:item.module.damage}: both parts.
Multiply by charge (melee only): both parts; full charge is ×1.
Roll the crit: physical part only (see [[combat/crit]]).
Multiply by bane: both parts (see [[combat/bane]]).
Add up: that is this hit's damage, never below 0.
Roll status procs: apply status effects to the target (see [[combat/element_status]]).

blocks.text: After the Hit

items: On a ranged hit with {lang:item.module.bursting_radius}, other mobs around the target take <t>50%</t> of this hit as splash. <w>Splash only spares you</w> — pets and villagers get hit too.
Special attributes such as execution and buff removal resolve (see [[reference/weapon_attr_special]]).
If this hit is enough to kill, kill stacks +1 (see [[combat/kill_stack]]).
Only then do the target's armor, Protection, shield and other mods' reductions apply.

blocks.title: Easy Mistakes
blocks.text: What counts is the item in your main hand at the moment of impact: swap weapons while an arrow is in flight and the new weapon is used; shoot a bow from the off-hand and you still get the main-hand item's panel.
Advanced Details

rows: adds {lang:item.module.magicDamage} on top of the above

items: “Other projectile” covers spectral arrows, tridents, gun bullets and so on.
Counts as magic: vanilla magic-type damage.

items.text: Spell damage from other magic mods is recognised as magic too.

items: The base-damage kill stack bonus is added to the melee and ranged bonuses.
Splash never procs elements and never builds weapon kill stacks.

blocks.text: Final damage = Raw damage × (Physical mult + Elemental mult) × Bane mult

rows: the hit before this pipeline: weapon damage, charge, vanilla jump crits and enchantments such as Sharpness are already in it
(1 + sum of damage bonuses) × Base Damage × charge × crit tier multiplier
((1 + sum of damage bonuses) × Base Damage + {lang:item.module.baseDamageWhenNotCriticalStrike}) × charge
sum of elemental attributes × Base Damage × charge (crits do not apply)
melee = how charged the swing was (0 ~ 1, full charge = 1); always 1 for ranged

blocks.text: Vanilla already lowers raw damage for an uncharged swing; charge scales it down again on top of that. It only follows swings you make yourself (sweep hits use the same swing); pets and other attackers count as fully charged.

Debuffs on the target such as Magnetic, and Kuva enemies' resistances (see [[enemies/lich_resistance]]), are already applied to the raw damage. Status procs use this hit's physical part as their base.
TACZ gun bullets resolve as ranged hits and use {lang:item.module.projectileDamage}. Gun-only attributes: see [[tacz/tacz_gun_attributes]].

entries.title: Critical Hits
entries.summary: Crit chance, the three crit tiers and multipliers

blocks.text: A <hl>crit</hl> is a chance for a hit's physical damage to be multiplied by the <t>Critical Multiplier</t> (M below). Both the chance and the multiplier are on the weapon's stat panel.
{lang:item.module.criticalStrikeProbability} can go above 100%. The excess is not wasted — it upgrades your crits: yellow → orange → red, each tier hitting harder.

rows: roll for a <c:FFFF55>yellow crit ×M</c>, otherwise no crit
at least yellow; the part above 100% is the chance of an <c:FFAA00>orange crit ×2M</c>
at least orange; the part above 200% is the chance of a <c:FF5555>red crit ×3M</c>

blocks.title: Example
blocks.text: M = 2.5 at 150% crit chance → half your hits deal ×2.5, half deal ×5. At exactly 100% / 200% / 300% you are guaranteed yellow / orange / red.
In Warframe, crit chance can also exceed 100%, and crit numbers turn from yellow to orange to red as the tier rises. “Red crits” are tier 3 and above.
Raising Your Crits

items: The base crit chance and multiplier are on the stat panel, rolled at random when the weapon was <t>consecrated</t> and got its panel; see [[weapons/weapon_panel]].
<t>Mods</t> (weapon upgrade cards) with crit chance or crit multiplier attributes raise the base values by a percentage.
Swing melee weapons at full charge: below full charge, crit chance is scaled down by the charge (damage multipliers too, see [[combat/damage]]) — spam-clicking almost never crits.
Sprinting melee attacks also get {lang:item.module.dashMeleeCriticalStrikeProbability}.
<w>Crits only boost the physical part</w>; elemental damage ignores the crit multiplier.

blocks.text: Advanced Details

rows: base crit chance × charge × (1 + {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeCriticalStrikeProbability}, plus {lang:item.module.dashMeleeCriticalStrikeProbability} while sprinting)
base crit multiplier × (1 + {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeCriticalStrikeMultiplier}) × (1 + melee crit damage stacks)

items: Status DoTs use the physical part as their base, so a crit hit applies a stronger DoT.
On a non-crit, the hit gains {lang:item.module.baseDamageWhenNotCriticalStrike}; on melee hits this bonus is scaled by charge too.

items.text: TACZ splits each bullet into two damage instances (normal + armor-piercing); when both deal damage, each rolls its own crit.
The two instances show as one damage number in the higher tier's color (see [[combat/damage_numbers]]).

entries.title: Bane
entries.summary: Bonus damage against specific mob types

blocks.text: Bane attributes (players often call them “discrimination”) make you hit one type of mob harder. Each hit only looks at the target's own type and uses that one attribute:

rows: most mobs: players, creepers, endermen, villagers, witches, ravagers, iron golems…
zombies, skeletons, phantoms, the Wither; <hl>this mod's enemies {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave} and {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} count too</hl>
spiders, cave spiders, silverfish, endermites, bees
guardians, squid, fish, dolphins; <w>no attribute of their own, they use the Illager one</w>

blocks.text: “Unknown” does not mean rare — it is simply the type for mobs nobody assigned one to. Most mobs from other mods fall here too, unless their author set a type.

blocks.title: Fighting Kuva Enemies
blocks.text: This mod's two enemies, the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave} and the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} (the boss), are both <t>undead</t>: stack {lang:item.module.bane_of_undead}. Element tips are at the end.
Warframe has faction mods, such as Bane of Grineer, that add damage against one enemy faction. Here the factions are replaced by Minecraft mob types.
Advanced Details
Bane multiplier = 1 + sum of bane attributes for the target's type

items: Physical and elemental parts are both multiplied; splash inherits the main target's result.
Status damage (DoTs, Electricity, Blast) uses the already-baned physical part as its base and multiplies by bane again — effectively squared: +50% bane becomes ×2.25 on that damage.
Negative bane lowers damage, but only against that type; other types are unaffected. Damage bottoms out at 0.

items.text: Elements against Kuva enemies: Electricity proc damage is ×1.5 against undead (see [[combat/element_status]]).

items: Elements against Kuva enemies: Heat DoT is halved on undead, and the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} is <w>fire-immune</w>, so Heat only strips its armor (see [[combat/element_status]]).

entries.title: Elements & Combinations
entries.summary: 13 damage types, combos and status procs

blocks.text: <hl>Elements</hl> are damage types added to your attacks, such as Heat, Cold and Electricity. Elemental attributes do two things: they add <t>elemental damage</t> to every hit, and they decide which status a <t>status proc</t> applies.

<t>Status proc</t>: based on {lang:item.module.triggerChance}, the hit applies a status effect to the target, such as burning, slowing or poison (see [[combat/element_status]]). There are 13 elements:
Pairs of the four base elements combine automatically into a combined element:
Warframe works the same way: Heat, Cold, Electricity and Toxin combine in pairs, and the result depends on the order of your mods. Building a weapon often means shuffling that order.
Combination Order

items: Queue up: a <t>Kuva weapon</t> (a boss drop) puts its innate element first.
The rest follow the order of the <t>mod</t> (upgrade card) slots on the weapon; within one mod, attribute order.
An element that appears more than once merges into its first position.
Walk front to back: each base element combines with the first earlier base element that is not yet combined and forms a valid pair.
Physical and already-combined elements never combine; a base element with no partner stays as it is.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} (slot 1), {lang:kuvaweapon.type.ice} (slot 2), {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity} (slot 3) → the first two become {lang:kuvaweapon.type.explosion} and {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity} is left alone: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.explosion} + {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity}. Want {lang:kuvaweapon.type.radiation}? Move {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity} ahead of {lang:kuvaweapon.type.ice}.
Status Chance

items: Above 100%, the whole-number part is guaranteed procs and the remainder rolls once more: 250% = 2 guaranteed + 50% for a third.
Each proc picks one element at random, weighted by each element's share: the bigger the share, the likelier the pick.
Combining only changes what can be picked. Total elemental damage never changes — it is always the plain sum of all elemental attributes.

blocks.title: Easy Mistakes
blocks.text: A weapon with no element on itself (innate Kuva element included) never procs, however high its status chance. Whatever you want to proc has to be on the weapon itself.
Advanced Details
Status chance = weapon base status chance × (1 + {lang:item.module.triggerChance}, plus {lang:item.module.dashTriggerChance} while sprinting) × (1 + status chance stacks)

items: At most <t>5</t> procs per hit — nothing gained past 500%.
Everyone's hits combined can proc at most <t>100</t> times per tick (1/20 s): when a big crowd is hit at once, the last ones may miss out.

items.text: Elemental attributes in extra slots such as the off-hand (see [[modules/multi_slot]]) only add elemental damage (including proc damage of the same element) — they do <w>not</w> add new elements to the proc pool.

entries.title: Status Effects
entries.summary: What each element does when it procs

blocks.text: When a status procs, the target gets the picked element's effect: some deal damage over time, some weaken the target. Effects first; the exact damage math is at the end.

rows: 1 + {lang:item.module.triggerTime}; sets how long effects last. Without that attribute t = 1, so “6t s” means 6 seconds
yellow hearts (absorption) on the target, whether from a Warframe shield or a golden apple (see [[warframe/shield]]). Most mobs have none

blocks.text: Damaging Elements

rows: Sets the target on fire and burns it every second; also strips armor and toughness step by step
Poison damage every second. If the target has a shield it skips the shield and hits health directly

cells: One instant shock plus paralysis (−99% movement speed)
A proc does nothing: no damage and no paralysis

rows: Damages health directly every second, ignoring armor, shield and i-frames
Leaves a 3-block-radius cloud at the hit point that damages every mob inside each second
Blasts the target and every mob within 3 blocks of it; no block damage

blocks.text: Debuff Elements

rows: Slows movement, attack and flying speed
The target <g>deals less damage</g>: melee, arrows and other projectiles it fires all count; your hits on it are unaffected
Knocks the target back and pops it up slightly; more Impact pushes farther
The target goes berserk: it attacks nearby mobs of its own kind first, otherwise the nearest mob (possibly you)
While the target has a shield, all damage it takes is increased
At full stacks the target's max health is halved; makes Slash DoT hurt more

items: Proccing the same debuff again adds a stack and refreshes its duration.
A target only ever has one DoT of each element: a new proc just refreshes it — DoTs do not stack.
<g>Puncture weakens enemy damage</g>: while a mob carries Puncture, the damage it deals drops by 40%~70%, which helps a lot in tough fights.
Gas clouds and Blast hit friend and foe alike: apart from you, pets, villagers and other players in range get hurt too.

blocks.text: In Warframe, a {lang:kuvaweapon.type.slash} proc causes Bleed, which ignores armor and shields; {lang:kuvaweapon.type.magnetic} is the anti-shield element and {lang:kuvaweapon.type.corrosion} strips armor. This mod follows the same ideas.
Advanced Details

rows: this hit's physical part (crit and bane included)
total of that element's attributes; a combined element uses the sum of its two base elements, and the innate Kuva element counts too

blocks.text: Each hit = coefficient × Base × Element value × Bane

rows: arthropods ×1.5, undead ×0.5; fire-immune targets take no burn damage
×2 ~ ×4.25 more if the target has Viral

items: DoTs pulse once per second, ⌈6t⌉ pulses in total (6t rounded up).
{lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire}: the target burns for 6 s; the armor strip deepens about every 0.5 s (15% → 30% → 40% → 50%) and lasts 6t s.
{lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison}: without a shield it is magic damage; with a shield it goes straight to health, also ignoring armor and i-frames.

items.text: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity}: only hits the struck target; the lightning is visual only and ignites nothing.

items: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.slash}: its damage does not depend on the size of your Slash attributes.

{lang:kuvaweapon.type.gas}: the cloud stays where it was placed and does not follow the target; it is tied to the struck mob and fades at most one pulse after it dies. A new proc moves the cloud to the latest hit point.
A new proc of the same DoT refreshes the remaining pulses and keeps the higher per-pulse damage.

Per-stack increase: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.ice} +5%, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.puncture} +10%, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.radiation} +0.5, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.magnetic} +0.25, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.corrosion} +6%.
{lang:kuvaweapon.type.radiation}: the berserk target looks for victims within 24 blocks.
{lang:kuvaweapon.type.impact}: knockback strength = Impact element value × 3.
Electricity and Blast on the struck target are often partly eaten by vanilla hit invulnerability (smaller or missing numbers); nearby mobs are not affected by this.
These statuses are not potion effects: they do not show in the effect list and do not count as “debuffs” for kill stacks (see [[combat/kill_stack]]).

items.text: Elemental attributes in extra slots such as the off-hand count toward the element value too.

blocks.title: Gas / Blast Attribute Trap
blocks.text: The proc damage of Gas and Blast only counts {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} + {lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison} (Gas) or {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} + {lang:kuvaweapon.type.ice} (Blast) attributes plus the innate Kuva element. Attributes that literally read Gas Damage / Blast Damage only add hit damage and raise the pick chance — with nothing but those on the weapon, a Gas or Blast proc deals no proc damage.

entries.title: Kill Stacks
entries.summary: Temporary buffs from kill streaks, and how they decay

blocks.text: Attributes marked “Gained on kill” are <hl>kill stacks</hl>: each kill adds 1 stack, more stacks mean a stronger effect, and they slowly fall off when you stop killing.
Stacks are stored on you, not on the weapon: switch to another weapon with the same stack attribute and your current stacks still apply.

items: Holding a <t>consecrated</t> weapon (one with a panel that can hold mods) with stack attributes, land a <t>lethal</t> hit (or trigger an execution) → every stack type the weapon carries gains 1 and its timer restarts.

With no new kills you lose 1 stack every interval, one at a time: weapon stacks <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.weaponStackDecayTicks|sec}</t>, Warframe stacks (see below) <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.warframeStackDecayTicks|sec}</t>.
Logging out clears everything; dying does not.

rows: melee and ranged damage bonus + value × stacks × number of debuffs on the target
{lang:item.module.firing_rate} + value × stacks; doubled for bows and crossbows

blocks.title: Base Damage Stack Trap
blocks.text: Its bonus is multiplied by the number of debuffs on the target, and only potion-style debuffs count (Slowness, Weakness, Poison, Wither and so on, other mods' ones included). This mod's element statuses do not count. With none on the target, even max stacks give +0.

items: A stack type only builds while your weapon carries that stack attribute.
The weapon panel shows the current stacks of each type (see [[weapons/weapon_panel]]).

blocks.text: Warframe has on-kill stacking mods too, such as the Galvanized series: kills stack up Multishot or damage bonuses for a while.
Warframe Stacks

<t>Warframe mods</t> are mods installed in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table} that boost you yourself. They have kill-stack attributes too (12 kinds: health, shield, armor, resistances…) with the same rules, but they build more easily:

items: Any killing blow credited to you counts: melee, arrows, bullets or splash; any weapon, consecrated or not.
Whether the hit was lethal is judged on the real damage after armor and shield.
Kills by element DoTs, Electricity or Blast still do not count.
Effects and caps: see [[reference/warframe_attr_killstack]].

blocks.text: Advanced Details

items: The weapon-stack kill check asks whether this hit's computed damage (before armor and shield) is at least the target's remaining health — so now and then you gain a stack while the mob survives.
Kills by element DoTs, Electricity, Blast or splash do not count for weapon stacks.

items.text: Stack attributes in extra slots such as the off-hand (see [[modules/multi_slot]]) count too: if the weapon or one of those slots carries it, that type builds.

entries.title: Damage Numbers
entries.summary: Colors, icons and merging of damage numbers

blocks.text: When you deal damage with a <t>consecrated</t> weapon (one with a panel that can hold mods), a number floats up from the target and stays for about 2 seconds. Its color tells you whether the hit crit:

rows: no crit; elemental damage is white too, followed by element icons
no crit, but the target has a shield (yellow hearts)

items: The number is the health actually lost: armor, resistances, other mods' reductions and hit invulnerability are already taken off, and damage absorbed by a shield is included.
Higher crit tiers use bigger text: white is smallest, then yellow / blue, then orange, and red is biggest.

items.text: Damage from unconsecrated weapons shows white numbers too.
Damage from unconsecrated weapons shows no numbers.
Every hit shows its own number.
Every hit shows its own number.

blocks.text: Icons Next to Numbers

items: Element icons after a hit number: which debuff elements this hit applied (Cold, Puncture, Impact, Radiation, Magnetic, Corrosive, Viral).
Shield icon: part of the hit landed on a shield.
Damaging elements (Heat, Toxin, Electricity, Slash, Gas, Blast) add no icon to the hit number; each floats its own white number with the matching element icon instead.

items.text: Dagger icon: direct health loss from {lang:item.module.true_bullet}; on its own it shows in <c:AA00AA>purple</c>.

items: Ribbon icon (in front of the number): damage your tamed creatures (maids, for example) deal with consecrated weapons is shown to you too; their elemental damage numbers are not shown.

blocks.text: Merged Numbers

items: Numbers on the same mob within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mergeDamageWindowMs} ms</t> merge into one: values add up, the color takes the highest tier and icons are combined.
Elemental damage only merges with numbers of the same element, never into hit numbers.

items.text: {lang:item.module.true_bullet} numbers usually fold into that shot's hit number, which turns purple if it was not a crit.

blocks.text: Advanced Details

items: Nothing shows when a hit is fully blocked (hit invulnerability, immunity, shield block).
When numbers get too dense some are dropped — actual damage is unaffected.
